summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26: FY26 sales grew 13.4%, EBITDA/kg rose to INR40.7 from INR37.6; management guides FY27 EBITDA of at least INR210 crore vs INR173 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 sales growth of about 13.4% with Pharma up over 200% and Paints double-digit growth, offset by a sharp fall in Lubes after losing BPCL business. Hyderabad consolidation from 5 units to 2 (Unit 1 and Unit 10) lifted margins, with EBITDA margin up about 8.4% and EBITDA per kg at INR40.7 versus INR37.6. Raw material (polypropylene) spiked from about INR105 to INR145-160 per kg during March after the West Asia war, and management says the full price rise has been passed through, though with a lag. Management guides FY27 value growth of 13-15% and volume growth of 10-13%, with capex cut to INR80-85 crore and ROCE targeted at 13.5-14% in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: about 219% YoY from about INR10.7 crore

financial_highlights.value: grew 37% over Q4 last year (value not stated)

financial_highlights.change: FY27 target at least INR210 crore (about 20% growth)

financial_highlights.value: about INR123 crore (INR72 crore plus INR59 crore cited, per call)
Q4 about 75.5% by volume; FY26 75.13% by volume, 76.8% by value

financial_highlights.metric: Food and FMCG thin wall value growth FY26

financial_highlights.value: up more than 60% in Q4 (about 10% of Paint growth contribution)

segments.name: Paints
segments.commentary: Paint grew double digits in FY26; ABG volumes up over 60% in Q4 and contributed about 10 points of the 14% Paint growth, Asian Paints added about 4 points. Paints and square packs EBITDA cited at INR30-35/kg.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about INR34.3 crore, up about 219%; FY27 target INR50-55 crore (50% growth). Capacity about 1,500 tonnes, planned 2,500 tonnes this year per management, with 1,000-1,200 tonnes additions cited for FY27.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Sharp decline after losing BPCL, which contributed INR14-15 crore in FY25 and went to L1 tendering. Lubes is about 17-18% of turnover; management sees no major growth and believes PSU losses are complete.

segments.name: Food and FMCG / Qpack
segments.commentary: Qpack grew about 25% and Food and FMCG over 15% in FY26. Panipat thin wall plant is at about 20-25% utilisation; March 2026 sales from Qpack and thin wall were a couple of crore, and new North-region sales of INR35-40 crore are expected in FY27.

segments.name: Grasim (ABG) capacity
segments.commentary: About 12,000 tonnes created across Panipat (5,000), Cheyyar (4,400) and Mahad/Satara (2,500), running at about 65% utilisation versus the 50s last year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth 13-15%; volume growth 10-13% (Pharma adds few tonnes); FY27 sales may cross INR1,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA at least INR210 crore vs INR173 crore in FY26 (about 20% growth); EBITDA per kg target 42.5-43 in FY27 and 43-45 in FY28.
ROCE expected at 13.5-14% in FY27 and around 15% by FY28, versus 17-18% two to three years ago.
Capex planned at INR80-85 crore in FY27 (brownfield only, Mysore and Satara/Mahad), down from about INR120 crore in FY26; management does not expect debt to rise.
Food and FMCG thin wall growth at least 20% in FY27 with Panipat adding 4 machines in July 2026 (thin wall capacity up about 100%).
capex_capacity: Total capacity about 63,000 MTPA with utilisation around 43,000 tonnes; management expects 67,000-70,000 MTPA by end of FY27.
Panipat: 4 thin wall machines coming in July 2026; second building for Food and FMCG has 4 machines, rising to 8 from July. Panipat ABG plant about 60% utilised; thin wall about 20-25%.

New Pharma plant on land at Sultanpur (earmarked for Pharma only): land possession expected this month; construction 8-9 months after handover; commercial production expected in FY27 before year-end, delayed from Q3 FY27 timeline.
Pharma capacity about 1,500 tonnes, targeted 2,500 tonnes this year; Food and FMCG Panipat capacity to reach about 2,000 tonnes, and 2,000-2,500 tonnes including Qpack.
Vibe collaboration: 2 of 3 closure designs have pilot molds ready; commercial revenue expected toward end of FY27 after 2-3 quarters.
demand_pricing: Raw material price rose from about INR105/kg to INR160/kg in March 2026 and is now about INR145-150/kg; management says the full price rise was passed through, and clients now reset prices monthly or fortnightly.
Clients returned to Mold-Tek on supply reliability: Berger and Nerolac increased call-ups, which began in March; Reliance supply normalised from mid-March.
Asian Paints volume growth 17% in Q4 after being negative through Q3; ABG volumes up over 60% YoY. Management expects double-digit growth from Asian Paints in coming years, driven by metallic IML.
BPCL Lubes business lost on L1 tendering; management sees no further PSU volume at risk.
Management says 98-99% of clients are blue chip; non-blue-chip exposure 4-7% of sales, with a potential 1-2% loss.
Management cited April 2026 as strong, despite the West Asia conflict, with paints and dairy/ice-cream demand intact.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Vibe collaboration contribute revenue in Q4, and is Pharma FY27 guidance inclusive of it?
qa_highlights.answer: No material Vibe revenue yet; 2 of 3 products have pilot molds, and commercial revenue expected toward end FY27. The INR55 crore Pharma target is separate, with the FY26 base about INR34.4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Lubes fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: BPCL, which contributed INR14-15 crore in FY25, was lost on L1 tendering as management did not match pricing. Lubes is 17-18% of turnover and no growth is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capacity utilisation and capex planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 63,000 tonnes and utilisation about 43,000 tonnes; FY27 capex is INR80-85 crore, all brownfield. Capacity may reach 67,000-70,000 tonnes by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 Paint growth a one-off, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a one-off. Paint value grew 13.5-14.4%; ABG grew over 60% and Asian Paints 17% in Q4, with Berger and Nerolac contributing only in the last weeks of March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time preventive maintenance cost for changing screws and parts to process RCP (recycled plastic) mandated at 30% now and 40% from April 2027; this is booked in the P&L.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor and inventory days stretched due to Pharma's 90-110 day payment cycle and 3 months of inventory; ROCE 12.4% in FY26, targeted 13.5-14% in FY27 and about 15% in FY28.

risks_watch: Polypropylene price volatility and the West Asia conflict; management says price pass-through is monthly or fortnightly, so margins could lag on price declines.
Lubes volume loss beyond BPCL and continued stagnation in the lubricant industry (17-18% of turnover).
Delay in Sultanpur Pharma plant land handover; commercial production slipped to FY27 year-end.
Panipat thin wall utilisation at about 20-25% and the July 2026 machine additions; North-region ramp-up depends on client wins.
Working capital stretch from Pharma's 90-110 day payment terms and higher-cost raw material inventory.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, Paints recovery and FY27 EBITDA; management was more hedged on the Lubes outlook, the timing of the Pharma plant and the impact of the war on demand. Several answers were revised or corrected during Q&A (volume growth 10-13%, not 10-15%).
key_quotes: And especially the consolidation of 5 units in Hyderabad into 2 units, that is Unit 1 and 10, has improved the overall performance and efficiencies and resulted in better EBITDA margins.
So we have taken a 50% growth to reach somewhere around close to between INR50 crores and INR55 crores for the Pharma.
But Lube being a laggard, that's why we are aiming between 10% to 13% volume growth.
We are aiming at, at least INR210 crores EBITDA for next financial year, up from INR173, that's 20% price.

adds.what: 4 thin wall machines at Panipat (Food and FMCG)
New Pharma plant at Sultanpur, targeting 2,500 tonnes Pharma capacity (vs ~1,500 t today)
Total capacity to 67,000-70,000 MTPA by end FY27 (from ~63,000 MTPA)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 13-15% value growth (10-13% volume) and EBITDA of at least INR210 crore vs INR173 crore, backed by 4 Panipat thin wall machines due July 2026, Sultanpur Pharma plant (delayed to FY27 year-end), and ~63,000 to 67,000-70,000 MTPA capacity by FY27-end against ~43,000 t utilised, but capex cut to INR80-85 crore and many growth elements are unquantified.
